human_messages: Hard-baked positive adaptation memory: repeated successful patterns become defaults; do not reset proven preferences or workflows each session.

Hard-baked secondary verification: for audits/reviews/validation, run a Claude pass when local checks still leave material uncertainty or a second read would materially improve trust; draft the prompt directly.

Hard-baked direct-launch rule: when a needed local surface exists as a terminal command or repo script, run it directly instead of asking the user to launch it; prefer direct launches for local Claude/OpenClaw/Yuri surfaces when they help review, audit, validation, or workflow continuity.

Advanced the LLM wiki by adding a wiki-facing source-registry mirror from the research archive, updating the wiki index from SOURCE_REGISTRY_MISSING to SOURCE_REGISTRY_MIRRORED, and keeping RAG ingestion deferred.
Remember to answer model guidance with exact model and reasoning only; omit platform labels and extra explanation unless explicitly requested.

Model selection is assistant-owned: choose the exact model and reasoning level per task from the local registry; do not ask the user to pick unless capability is missing or the choice changes the outcome materially.

Hard-baked routing hierarchy: pick the offload lane first, then choose the exact model and reasoning for the current phase; allow model switches at task or phase boundaries; use gpt-5.4-mini medium by default, gpt-5.5 high for synthesis/review/risk/final decisions, and gpt-5.3-codex-spark only for exact-scope micro-work.

Hard-baked coupling rule: offload routing and model routing are one coordinated system; keep lane and model aligned automatically during background work, with lane first and phase-boundary model switches only.
